title: Per-team lifecycle overlay for shared corpus roles: one team's close is not all
acceptance: Seeded corpus job X (workspace_id NULL, status NULL). closeRoleIfOpen(X, 'wsA') -> true; afterwards listCorpusJobs('wsB') still contains X and listCorpusJobs('wsA') does not; the jobs row's own status column is still NULL.
closeRoleIfOpen(X, 'wsA') called twice -> true, then false (the compare-and-swap holds per team in the overlay, so the role-fill hook still runs its withdrawal sweep at most once per team).

setJobStatus(X, 'published', 'wsA') on a corpus row writes no jobs.status/published_at; classifyPublish(X, 'wsB') afterwards -> { already: false, billable: true } (each team's first go-live of a corpus role is its own metered event, not a free ride on team A's published_at).

setRoleOpenConfig(X, { targetHires: 3, postingLangs: ['cs'] }, 'wsA'); getRoleOpenConfig(X, 'wsB') -> { targetHires: 1, postingLangs: [] } and getRoleOpenConfig(X, 'wsA') -> { targetHires: 3, postingLangs: ['cs'] }.

After wsA closes X: countOpenRoles('wsA').corpus is one lower than countOpenRoles('wsB').corpus, and countJobs({ openOnly: true }, 'wsB') is unchanged from before the close; listJobsPage({}, 'wsB') decorates X with status null while listJobsPage({}, 'wsA') decorates it 'closed'.
Authored job Y (workspace_id 'wsA'): setJobStatus(Y, 'closed', 'wsA') updates jobs.status exactly as today and inserts NO overlay row (the overlay is only for workspace_id NULL rows).
Legacy corpus row whose jobs.status was already 'closed' before the migration, with no overlay row -> reads 'closed' for every team (the base value is kept, never guessed into one team's overlay).

Tenancy: the overlay table is listed as workspace-scoped in app/_lib/tenancy.ts and every SQL statement touching it binds workspace_id (source guard with an EMPTY exemption list, same shape as role-priorities-tenancy.test.ts).
premise: app/_lib/db/jobs.ts:853-855 names the defect as a deliberate residual: 'the `status` column on a seeded row is itself shared, so one tenant closing a corpus role affects all - that needs per-tenant lifecycle state on shared rows, not an ownership check.'
app/_lib/db/jobs.ts:856-858 canWriteJobLifecycle lets every tenant write the lifecycle of a seeded corpus row (owner NULL -> visible -> writable).
app/_lib/db/jobs.ts:684-689 closeRoleIfOpen(id) is `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'closed' WHERE id = ? AND (status IS NULL OR status = 'published')` - keyed by id alone, no workspace.

app/_lib/stage-hooks-role-fill.ts:103-108 the post-commit auto-close fires after ONE team's hires reach target: hired = listJobPipelineStats(workspaceId)[jobId].hired; target = getRoleOpenConfig(jobId); then closeRoleIfOpen(jobId) - so one team's first hire on a corpus role (target NULL folds to 1 at jobs.ts:619-621) closes it for every team.

app/_lib/db/jobs.ts:638-661 getRoleOpenConfig(id)/setRoleOpenConfig(id, ...) read/write target_hires + posting_langs on the shared row by id: team A publishing with targetHires 3 sets team B's target.

app/_lib/job-ingest.ts:167-179 setJobStatus(jobId, status) is a by-id UPDATE of jobs.status and published_at; app/_lib/job-ingest.ts:196-201 classifyPublish derives billable from the shared published_at, so the second team to adopt a corpus role is never metered.
app/_lib/db/jobs.ts:917-927 listCorpusJobs filters `(status IS NULL OR status = 'published')` on the shared column, so a corpus role closed by team A disappears from team B's rematch corpus.

app/api/jobs/[id]/close/route.ts:30-38 the manual close: canWriteJobLifecycle then setJobStatus(id, 'closed') - withdrawal is scoped to the caller (closeEntriesByJobId(id, ws)) but the status flip is global, so team B's in-flight candidates are left on a role B can no longer receive applications for.

app/_lib/tenancy.ts:157-163 (role_pattern_priorities), :197-204 (interview_kits) and :301-306 (job_translations) already key per-team state on a possibly-shared corpus job as (workspace_id, job_id) for exactly this reason - 'a job-only key would both leak one team's private weighting of a role and let the next team overwrite it'. Lifecycle state is the one per-team fact about a corpus role still stored on the shared row.
rollback: The series is additive: one CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS migration plus read folds (COALESCE(overlay.status, jobs.status)) and write routing for workspace_id-NULL rows only. Reverting the commits restores the by-id writes and leaves the overlay table unread; authored rows were never written through it. What a revert loses is honest and bounded: per-team closes/targets of corpus roles recorded during the window stop applying (those roles read by their base status again) - no row is rewritten, so no data has to be migrated back.
runner_up: Fork-on-adopt: copy a corpus role into an authored row when a team publishes it - rejected because job ids key pipeline_entries, interview_kits, job_translations and dev_cases.job_id, so a fork would orphan every link already made to the corpus id.
body:
## Summary
The seeded jobs corpus is shared by every team, but a role's lifecycle - live/closed, hire target, posting languages, first-publish stamp - is stored on that shared row. One team hiring one candidate on a corpus role auto-closes it for every team. Move the per-team half of the lifecycle into a (workspace_id, job_id) overlay, the same shape kits, translations and role priorities already use.

## Description
`jobs.ts:853-855` records this as a known residual. It is live today: the role-fill hook (`stage-hooks-role-fill.ts:103-108`) closes a role once `hired >= target`. It counts hires per team but closes the row by id (`closeRoleIfOpen`, `jobs.ts:684-689`). Because a corpus role's target folds to 1 (`jobs.ts:619-621`), team A's first hire takes the role out of team B's apply doors, catalog and rematch corpus (`listCorpusJobs`, `jobs.ts:917-927`). None of team B's in-flight candidates are withdrawn. The same shared row also carries `target_hires`/`posting_langs` (`jobs.ts:638-661`) and the `published_at` stamp that billing uses (`job-ingest.ts:196-201`), so team B's adoption of a corpus role is never metered.

The move adds a `job_workspace_state(workspace_id, job_id, status, published_at, target_hires, posting_langs, PK(workspace_id, job_id))` table. Writes for rows whose `jobs.workspace_id IS NULL` route to the overlay: `setJobStatus`, `closeRoleIfOpen` (the CAS moves into the overlay UPSERT's WHERE), `setRoleOpenConfig`, and `classifyPublish`'s stamp. Writes for authored rows stay exactly as they are. Reads fold with `COALESCE(overlay.x, jobs.x)` in `listJobsPage`, `countJobs`, `countOpenRoles`, `listCorpusJobs`, `getRoleOpenConfig`, `getJobStatus` and an optional-workspace `getJob`. The tenant predicate stays literal in each template, because `jobs-tenancy.test.ts` greps for it. Public apply doors keep calling `getJobStatus(id)`. Its default resolves the tenant through `getJobWorkspace(id)`, which is the team a public applicant is filed into, so those routes do not change.

## Flow
1. Migration in core.ts: create the overlay and add it to the tenancy manifest as scoped (no exemptions).
2. job-ingest.ts: `setJobStatus(jobId, status, workspaceId)`, `getJobStatus(jobId, workspaceId?)` and `classifyPublish(jobId, workspaceId)` branch on the row's tier.
3. jobs.ts: fold the overlay into every status/target read. `closeRoleIfOpen(id, ws)` and `get/setRoleOpenConfig(id, ws)` become per-team.
4. stage-hooks-role-fill.ts, the close route and the publish route pass the team they already hold. The publish transaction keeps its single-connection atomicity.
5. Tests first: 8 behaviour cases plus a tenancy guard. docs/features/jobs/README.md states the two-tier lifecycle.

## Expected impact
A whole class of cross-team interference closes: auto-close, manual close, re-publish and target setting on a shared role. That covers every team using the default corpus, which is every install. One team's hire stops silently darkening a role another team is still hiring for, and adopting a corpus role becomes a metered event for each team that adopts it. The residual note in jobs.ts is deleted instead of carried.

## Evaluation
Claim: a corpus role's lifecycle is per-team, and authored roles are unchanged.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test cases in app/_lib/db/job-workspace-state.test.ts + job-workspace-state-tenancy.test.ts, then the integration gate (tsc, lint, test:unit incl. jobs-tenancy + role-fill tests, test:perf).
Result: pending build.
Gate: architecture (new persistent table + tenancy manifest entry).
evidence:
jobs.ts:853-855: "(Residual, deliberately out of scope: the `status` column on a seeded row is itself shared, so one tenant closing a corpus role affects all - that needs per-tenant lifecycle state on shared rows, not an ownership check.)"
jobs.ts:686: `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'closed' WHERE id = ? AND (status IS NULL OR status = 'published')`
stage-hooks-role-fill.ts:106-108: `const hired = listJobPipelineStats(workspaceId)[jobId]?.hired ?? 0; const target = roleTargetHires(getRoleOpenConfig(jobId).targetHires); if (hired < target) ...; if (!closeRoleIfOpen(jobId)) ...`
jobs.ts:620: roleTargetHires folds NULL -> 1.
jobs.ts:639: `SELECT target_hires, posting_langs FROM jobs WHERE id = ?`; jobs.ts:659: `UPDATE jobs SET target_hires = COALESCE(?, target_hires), posting_langs = COALESCE(?, posting_langs) WHERE id = ?`
job-ingest.ts:174/178: `UPDATE jobs SET status = ?, published_at = COALESCE(published_at, ?) WHERE id = ?` / `UPDATE jobs SET status = ? WHERE id = ?`
job-ingest.ts:201: `billable: !r?.published_at`
jobs.ts:925: listCorpusJobs `WHERE (status IS NULL OR status = 'published') AND (workspace_id IS NULL OR workspace_id = ?)`
close/route.ts:31,38: `if (!canWriteJobLifecycle(id, ws)) ... setJobStatus(id, "closed");`
tenancy.ts:158-160: role_pattern_priorities "Scoped rather than job-keyed BECAUSE the jobs corpus is dual-tier: a seeded corpus role is shared by every tenant, so a job-only key would both leak one team's private weighting of a role and let the next team overwrite it."
Status-gate callers of getJobStatus/isJobOpenForApplications: 10 sites (apply x3, channels inbound, sim apply-cv, inbound-lead, apply pages x2, jds page, jds route) - all keep their signature via the defaulted workspace.

title: One interview-session transition table; late writes re-assert it
acceptance: Pure table: canInterviewTransition('revoked','in_progress') -> false; ('failed','in_progress') -> true; ('created','in_progress') -> true; ('completed', any) -> false; ('in_progress','revoked') -> true; an unknown from-status -> false.

markInterviewStarted on a session whose status is 'revoked' -> returns false and the row stays 'revoked' with started_at unchanged (today the WHERE is `status != 'completed'`, so it flips to in_progress).

completeInterviewSession(id, { status: 'completed', transcript }) on a row that was revoked AFTER the caller read it -> transcript is persisted, the stored status stays 'revoked', and the result reports the stored status so the route skips billing/scoring (the SQL keeps a revoke instead of the caller's stale pre-read).

attachInterviewScorecard on a completed session whose entry was erased in between (anonymizeEntry scrubbed transcript_json to '[]' and scorecard_json to NULL) -> refuses (applied false), scorecard_json stays NULL.
attachInterviewScorecard on a completed session with a non-empty transcript -> writes and reports applied true (the happy path is unchanged).

setInterviewAgenda / setInterviewSessionProvider on a session revoked after connect started -> return false and write nothing; the connect route then answers INTERVIEW_LINK_INACTIVE (existing code) instead of returning freshly minted provider credentials.

Source guard: every `SET status=` statement in app/_lib/db/interviews.ts carries a status predicate, and each one is built from the transition table's from-set for its target. A hand-written `status != 'completed'` guard on a status write fails the test.
premise: app/_lib/db/interviews.ts:659-661 and :669-671 markInterviewStarted guards `WHERE id=? AND status != 'completed'` - a 'revoked' row is flipped back to 'in_progress', although revokeInterviewSession (:505) and the connect route (:124-126) treat revoked as terminal.

app/api/interview/connect/route.ts:234-237 calls markInterviewStarted the 'Atomic backstop for the check above', but it backstops only the completed case. The revoked check at :124 has no store-level twin.

app/api/interview/connect/route.ts:290-418 awaits kit builds (buildInterviewKit :290, buildGroundedInterview :301, buildKitOnlyInterviewKit :328, buildCandidateSafeBrief :381) and the provider connect (connectWithFailover :418) AFTER markInterviewStarted at :237, then hands credentials to the browser. A recruiter revoke (revokeOpenInterviewSessions, app/api/interview/revoke/route.ts:25) in that window does not stop the mint. The only later writes, setInterviewSessionProvider (:447) and setInterviewAgenda, guard `status != 'completed'` (interviews.ts:725, :737) and so accept a revoked row.

app/api/interview/complete/route.ts:232 derives the final status from a pre-read (`session.status === 'revoked' ? 'revoked' : ...`), and interviews.ts:694 writes it with `WHERE id=? AND status != 'completed'`. A revoke landing after the read (by another process, since better-sqlite3 serializes in-process) is overwritten to 'completed'. That undoes the lifecycle fact the comment at complete/route.ts:213-231 calls load-bearing.

app/_lib/db/interviews.ts:1049-1057 attachInterviewScorecard is an unguarded `UPDATE interview_sessions SET scorecard_json=?, updated_at=? WHERE id=?`, called at complete/route.ts:419 after `await runInterviewScorecard(...)` (:402, an LLM synthesis). app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:2234-2237 (scrubEntryLinkedPii, reached from anonymizeEntry :2391) sets transcript_json='[]' and scorecard_json=NULL because the scorecard 'is a free-text synthesis quoting them'. An erasure inside the scoring await is written back over by the late attach.

Four different spellings of the status guard live in one file: `IN ('created','in_progress','failed')` (:505, :524), `!= 'completed'` (:661, :671, :694, :725, :737, :750), `='in_progress'` (:493), and none (:1052). Nothing states which moves are legal. app/_lib/devcase-transitions.ts (97 lines) already solved the same shape for dev_lifecycle with a literal-array + edges table + canTransition used inside updateLifecycle's CAS (devcase.ts:355-376).
rollback: Additive and self-contained: a new pure module, WHERE clauses tightened on existing statements, and two route branches that refuse on a `false` the store already returns today. Reverting the commits restores the old predicates exactly. No schema change and no data rewrite, so there is nothing to migrate back.
runner_up: Move the whole-app comms outbox (dev_outbox: recordOutbox, listOutbox, listOutboxFiltered, getOutboxEntry, hasOutboxSendFor, outboxWorkspaceForRef - devcase.ts:494-652) out of the devcase store into its own db/outbox.ts. It is a real misplacement but a pure move, so impact is below 7.
body:
## Summary
`interview_sessions.status` is a five-state machine: created, in_progress, failed, completed, revoked. Nothing states which moves between them are legal. Ten UPDATEs in interviews.ts each hand-write their own guard, and three of those guards are wrong in the same direction: they treat `revoked` as live. Write the edges down once, as devcase-transitions.ts does for dev_lifecycle, and derive every status write's WHERE from them. Then make the two writes that land after a long await (the post-connect writes and the scorecard attach) conditional writes whose `changes === 0` stops the effect.

## Description
The recruiter's Revoke is the one control over a live, paid credential on a public link. Three store writes can undo it or ignore it:
- `markInterviewStarted` (`:659-671`, guard `status != 'completed'`) reopens a revoked row.
- `completeInterviewSession` (`:694`) writes the caller's pre-read status over a revoke that landed after the read.
- The connect route awaits kit builds and the provider connect for seconds after the start (`connect/route.ts:290-418`). A revoke in that window still ends with fresh credentials in the browser, because the only later writes (`setInterviewSessionProvider`, `setInterviewAgenda`) also accept `revoked`.

Separately, `attachInterviewScorecard` (`:1049-1057`) has no guard at all. It runs after an awaited LLM synthesis, so a GDPR erasure that scrubbed the row during scoring is overwritten with a scorecard that quotes the erased candidate.

The fix follows the technique: when the irreversible step is a write to the store that holds the state, condition the write rather than re-read. `app/_lib/interview-session-status.ts` holds `INTERVIEW_SESSION_STATUSES`, `EDGES`, `canInterviewTransition` and `fromStatesFor(target)`. Each status UPDATE renders its `status IN (...)` from `fromStatesFor`. `completeInterviewSession` keeps a revoke with `status = CASE WHEN status = 'revoked' THEN 'revoked' ELSE ? END` and returns the stored status. `attachInterviewScorecard` requires `status = 'completed' AND transcript_json != '[]'` and returns `{ applied }`. The post-connect writes return `changes > 0`, and the connect route refuses with the existing INTERVIEW_LINK_INACTIVE code when they report the row left `in_progress`. No new error code or catalog key is needed.

## Flow
1. Tests first: the 7 cases above, in interview-session-status.test.ts and db/interview-session-transitions.test.ts.
2. Add the pure table module (literal array + derived union + runtime guard, the tabs.ts shape).
3. Rewrite the status predicates in interviews.ts from the table. Give the scorecard attach and the post-connect writes an applied result.
4. connect/route.ts refuses on a post-connect write that did not land. complete/route.ts skips the decision seal when the attach is refused, and bills and scores from the stored status.
5. docs/features/interviews/README.md gets the state table.

## Expected impact
Revoke stops the candidate from running the call: a revoked link can no longer be reopened, and credentials are no longer handed out across a revoke. An erased candidate's scorecard can no longer be written back by a late scoring run. The ten hand-written guards become one table that a source guard holds, so the next status writer cannot pick a sixth spelling.

## Evaluation
Claim: every interview_sessions status write obeys one transition table, and late writes cannot cross a revoke or an erasure.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass.
After: 7 of 7.
Method: gate - node:test over the pure module and the store on the isolated unit DB (testing/unit-db.ts), then the integration gate (tsc, lint, test:unit incl. interview-link-lifecycle, interview-failover-attempts, interviews-tenancy, error-message-hygiene).
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract (store return shapes change for attachInterviewScorecard / setInterviewSessionProvider; route behaviour tightens, no loosening).
